subject: Spike of 429s impacting CloudForge jobs — status & remediation
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudforge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@cloudforge.com
Date: 2026-05-02T09:12:30-07:00
Subject: Unexpected 429s impacting production - urgent

Hi Hannah / Marissa —

We started seeing a spike in 429s hitting our streaming jobs around 08:50 PDT (attached sample log = cloudforge-429-sample.log). Error rate is roughly 3–5% across a handful of routes and it's causing downstream retries and job backpressure.

Can you confirm status on your side and whether something changed with quota/rate limits this morning? We have a release window at 10:00 and this is blocking the run.

Alex Jenkins
CTO, CloudForge
alex.jenkins@cloudforge.com

Attachments: cloudforge-429-sample.log (text, 18 KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-02T09:18:05-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected 429s impacting production - urgent

Thanks Alex — looping in David + Sean to own the immediate remediation. Initial checks on infra show elevated 429 counts correlated with a rate-cap change that rolled out in the early morning (09:05) as part of a routing optimization. We're treating this as an incident.

Immediate plan (next 60 minutes):
- David: roll back the global cap and apply per-tenant caps so CloudForge traffic isn't subject to the new global limit (ETA 09:45).
- Marissa: notify account and coordinate a short maintenance window if needed.
- Sean: prepare a temporary credit offer and log retention snapshot.

I created INC-20260502 in the console and uploaded the initial logs. I'll update CloudForge as soon as we have confirmation the 429s are cleared.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachment: playbook-quicksteps.pdf (ops playbook excerpt)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudforge.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-02T09:44:17-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected 429s impacting production - status update

Alex / Hannah — quick update from the infra side. Root cause: an automated rollout pushed a conservative global rate cap at 09:05 which inadvertently throttled high-throughput tenants (CloudForge among them). That cap was intended for a small test cohort but a selector mismatch caused it to be applied more broadly.

Actions taken (09:12–09:43):
- Reverted the global cap (09:25).
- Applied a per-tenant cap configuration for CloudForge to match your pre-release profile (09:33).
- Increased short-term burst allowance for affected routes to smooth retries (09:40).

I've attached a diff of the quota change we rolled back (quota-change-diff.txt). Can you confirm if your jobs are seeing errors subside? We'll keep the monitoring window open for 2 hours and follow up with a full postmortem.

-David
David Kim
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

Attachment: quota-change-diff.txt (text)

From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudforge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudForge Support <support@cloudforge.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T10:01:02-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected 429s impacting production - confirmation

Thanks David — we see the 429 spike collapse back to baseline around 09:47 and the job queue has drained. Appreciate the quick rollback.

A couple asks while you investigate:
1) We need a formal postmortem with timeline and root cause (our compliance team will review).
2) Please confirm what SLA credit will be applied for the incident window (we logged failed job runs and customer-facing retries).
3) Can you share what guardrails will be added to prevent a rollout selector from affecting global config again?

If possible, we'd like the postmortem by EOD tomorrow and a follow-up 30-minute call to review.

Alex
Alex Jenkins
CTO, CloudForge

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-02T12:16:44-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — INC-20260502

Alex — thanks again for the quick signal and patience. We've completed the initial post-incident summary and attached the formal postmortem (postmortem-INC-20260502.pdf) to this thread and also published it to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/postmortems/INC-20260502.

Executive summary:
- Impact window: 09:05–09:47 PDT.
- Symptom: unexpected 429 responses from rate-limited endpoints affecting CloudForge's streaming jobs (3–5% error rate at peak).
- Root cause: rollout automation applied a conservative global rate cap due to a selector misconfiguration.
- Remediation: rollback of global cap (09:25), per-tenant caps and burst allowance applied (09:33–09:40).

Planned follow-up items:
- Deploy rollout selector validation checks in the pipeline (owner: infra team) — ETA 2 weeks.
- Add an automated canary that measures 429 delta vs. baseline post-deploy (owner: SRE) — ETA 10 days.
- Offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of CloudForge's May invoice for customer disruption (Sean will send formal credit request).

We propose a 30-minute call tomorrow (May 3) at 10:00 PDT to walk through the postmortem and action plan. Please confirm a time that works for you.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: postmortem-INC-20260502.pdf (formal report)
